THOUGHT: The patient is an elderly man with subacute, progressive symmetric weakness particularly of the legs, urinary retention (a cauda/conus/cord or radicular process), marked reduction of reflexes (a lower‑motor‑neuron/radicular or peripheral neuropathy picture), and moderate unilateral ptosis. Skin exam shows violaceous cutaneous lesions documented as “leukemia cutis.” MRI spine shows nodular thickening and enhancement of the lumbosacral nerve roots (cauda equina radiculopathy) with no intrinsic spinal cord lesion and heterogeneous marrow signal. CSF is massively abnormal with 3,397 WBC/µL and 98% atypical cells/blasts — this is diagnostic of malignant/leukemic leptomeningeal involvement rather than an inflammatory or typical infectious neuropathy (where CSF would show few cells or neutrophils). Taken together: (1) skin lesions consistent with leukemic infiltration, (2) abnormal marrow signal on MRI, and (3) blasts predominating in CSF with nerve‑root enhancement indicate leukemic infiltration of the leptomeninges and peripheral nerve roots (neuroleukemiosis / leukemic meningoradiculopathy). In an elderly patient leukemia cutis and extramedullary skin/chief infiltration are most often seen with acute myeloid leukemia (especially monocytic variants) and myeloid sarcoma/chloroma, although acute lymphoblastic leukemia or lymphomatous involvement can produce a similar picture. Other differentials (neurolymphomatosis from NHL, leptomeningeal carcinomatosis from solid tumor, infectious meningitis, inflammatory polyradiculoneuropathies) are far less likely given the CSF cytology and cutaneous/marrow findings.

DIAGNOSIS:
1. Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) with leptomeningeal and nerve‑root (radicular) infiltration — leukemic meningoradiculopathy / neuroleukemiosis (most likely given leukemia cutis, marrow signal change, and CSF blasts)
2. Acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) with meningeal/radicular involvement (less likely because of patient age but can present with CSF blasts and radiculopathy)
3. Neurolymphomatosis / leptomeningeal involvement from non‑Hodgkin lymphoma (malignant lymphomatous infiltration of nerves and CSF)
4. Leptomeningeal carcinomatosis from metastatic solid tumor (cauda equina/nerve‑root infiltration causing similar MRI and CSF findings)
5. Myeloid sarcoma (chloroma) / extramedullary AML involving skin and nerve roots (closely related to AML; an alternative formulation of extramedullary myeloid disease)
ground_truth: Blastic plasmacytoid dendritic cell neoplasm (BPDCN) with polyradiculopathy
